latest_release.name: v3.12.1
latest_release.body:
# Changelog

All notable changes to Chisle are documented here.
Format loosely follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/).

## [Unreleased]

## [3.12.1] - 2026-11-14

Patch: the Pi extension stops re-adding its rules every turn when a rules section is turned off, and Windows fixes from [@anhtahaylove](https://github.com/anhtahaylove).

### Fixed
- **Pi/OMP rules injected once with any `sections` config.** With `sections.code=false`, the extension no longer recognized its own rules in the system prompt and appended them again on every turn. It now also matches its `CHISLE ACTIVE` header plus `## Boundaries`, which the sections filter never drops. (#51)
- **`benchmarks/run-ablation.js` on Windows.** CRLF checkouts no longer crash the prompt parser. (#49)

### Tests
- The suite passes on Windows: symlink and file-mode checks skip only where the OS can't support them, and tests no longer read the developer's real config or `%APPDATA%`. (#50)

## [3.12.0] - 2026-11-13

Minor: native OpenCode v2 support, and `--update` now really updates the Claude Code plugin.

### Added
- **OpenCode v2 plugin compatibility.** The installer detects OpenCode's major version and installs an isolated `Plugin.define({ id, setup })` entrypoint for v2 while preserving the v1 plugin. V2 `shell` output uses the shared compressor, spill recovery, statistics, configuration, and safety exclusions. (#48, [@lextiz](https://github.com/lextiz))

### Fixed
- **`--update` updates the Claude Code plugin.** `npx chisle@latest --update` ran `claude plugin install`, which skips a plugin that is already installed, so Claude Code stayed on the previous release while the run reported success. When the plugin is present, `--update` and `--force` now run `claude plugin update chisle@chisle`. A regression test drives a fake `claude` CLI and checks the update path.

### Docs
- README, site and the benchmark chart label the current numbers as Chisle rather than Chisle 3.9.

## [3.11.1] - 2026-11-07

### Added
- **`npx chisle mcp wrap` covers Antigravity, Codex and GitHub Copilot in VS Code.** Antigravity: `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`. Copilot: the VS Code user `mcp.json` (Code, Code Insiders, VSCodium), keyed `servers`. Codex: `~/.codex/config.toml` (honors `CODEX_HOME`); only the `command`/`args` lines of `[mcp_servers.<name>]` tables change, tables with non-string values are skipped, and the original stays in `config.toml.chisle-bak`. Every agent Chisle supports now gets MCP output compression or more.

### Fixed
- An empty MCP config file reads as "no servers" instead of "not strict JSON".
- Site: the top border of hovered ladder cards is no longer clipped.

## [3.11.0] - 2026-11-07

Minor: `npx chisle tools` trims skill descriptions as well as tool schemas; README and site show correctness up front.

### Added
- **`npx chisle tools` trims skill descriptions too.** Every request carries the skill listing, a description per skill. Skills the model never invoked in the window are set to `skillOverrides: "name-only"`, which keeps them listed and callable by name; your own overrides are never touched, and `tools restore` undoes exactly what trim set. Measured on a fresh session with the maintainer's config: 65 unused skills name-only took the base request from 24,185 to 23,248 tokens; projects that ship more skills save more.

### Docs
- README and site lead with correctness next to cost: 156/156 vs bare 154/156 on auto-graded maths and coding, 38/42 vs 36/42 on agentic hidden-test repos, both ties (p = 0.498, 0.738). The site's stats show 156/156 in place of the zero-dependencies tile, which the hero already states.

## [3.10.0] - 2026-11-07

Minor: `npx chisle tools` trims unused tool schemas, and the benchmarks start over from the 3.9 runs.

### Added
- **`npx chisle tools`: trim unused tool schemas.** Claude Code sends every loaded tool's schema on every request. The command reads your transcripts and reports each heavy tool's schema size against your own

English · Español · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語

Fewer tokens than caveman and ponytail. No accuracy lost.

```bash npx chisle ```

See both answers
The prompt: *"Implement an order state machine covering created, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled and refunded, with the legal transitions enforced and invalid ones rejected."* Excerpts from the verbatim committed answers in [`raw-nov-sidebyside/large-s2`](benchmarks/results/raw-nov-sidebyside/large-s2/):
no ruleset: 121 lines, 1,186 answer tokensChisle: 62 lines, 530 answer tokens
```python class OrderStateError(Exception): """Raised when an invalid state transition is attempted.""" pass class Order: # Define valid transitions: state -> list of allowed next states VALID_TRANSITIONS = { … } def transition_to(self, next_state): """Transition to the next state. Raises OrderStateError if invalid.""" def can_transition_to(self, next_state): """Check if a transition is allowed without performing it.""" ``` …plus usage, tests, printed output and a recap of the transitions. ```python class OrderStateMachine: TRANSITIONS = { "created": {"pay", "cancel"}, "paid": {"ship", "refund", "cancel"}, … } def transition(self, event): if event not in self.TRANSITIONS[self.state]: raise ValueError(f"Cannot {event} from {self.state}. …") self.state = self.STATE_MAP[(self.state, event)] return self.state ``` Then a short usage block.

Every raw transcript is committed, losses included. Method and data · why we publish the losses

Other ways to install
```bash # Claude Code plugin marketplace claude plugin marketplace add JayPokale/Chisle claude plugin install chisle@chisle # curl curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayPokale/Chisle/main/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayPokale/Chisle/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` Per-agent setup, upgrading and config: [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md).
